decisions.reason: Product A has its own webpage and is a core pharmaceutical, so the firm's visible public commitment and sunk investment make dropping unlikely despite any early disappointment.
Product B is presented on its own page as a generic antidepressant, representing a central pharmaceutical commitment that management will justify by persisting.
Product C has its own page and is a combination antihypertensive, a core product with strong public commitment and sunk costs, so escalation leads to keeping it.
Product D is only mentioned on the website and is a peripheral dietary supplement, so lower visibility and investment mean weaker escalation pressure and a higher likelihood of discontinuation.
